title: User Stories — hii

sections.title: 1. Agile Methodology & Persona Mapping
sections.body:
This document outlines the user stories for the Hospital Management System (HMS), structured to support agile development cycles. The system is designed to provide a centralized platform for managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, and administrative functions. 

**Compliance & Security Context:**
All user stories involving patient data must adhere to HIPAA and GDPR standards. This includes ensuring PHI encryption at rest (AES-256), maintaining immutable audit trails, and meeting RTO < 1h / RPO < 5min benchmarks. HL7 FHIR and DICOM standards apply to medical record and imaging data exchange.

**Persona Mapping:**
Based on the source document, the following roles are identified as primary personas:
1. **Admin**: Manages system configuration, staff, and high-level reports.
2. **Doctor**: Manages appointments, diagnoses, prescriptions, and clinical notes.
3. **Nurse**: Manages patient care, vital signs, nursing notes, and bed status.
4. **Receptionist**: Handles patient registration, appointments, and queue management.
5. **Pharmacist**: Manages pharmacy inventory, prescriptions, and medicine dispensing.
6. **Lab Technician**: Processes laboratory test requests and generates reports.
7. **Accountant**: Manages billing, payments, insurance, and invoices.
8. **Patient**: Views appointments, prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history via a portal.

sections.title: 2. Epics & User Stories Matrix
table: As a user, I want to log in securely using JWT/OAuth so that my access is restricted to my role.
Ensures role-based access control and secure authentication.
As a receptionist, I want to register new patients and manage their profiles so that hospital records are centralized.
Facilitates efficient patient onboarding and data management.
As a receptionist, I want to schedule appointments and manage queues based on doctor availability so that patient wait times are minimized.
Improves operational efficiency and patient flow.
As a doctor, I want to view and update patient medical records, including diagnosis, prescriptions, and treatment history, so that I have a complete clinical picture.
Enhances clinical decision-making and continuity of care.
As a lab technician, I want to process test requests and generate reports so that diagnostic results are available promptly.
As a pharmacist, I want to manage medicine inventory and dispense prescriptions so that medication availability is tracked.
Prevents stockouts and ensures accurate dispensing.
As an accountant, I want to generate invoices, process payments, and manage insurance claims so that financial transactions are accurate.
As a patient, I want to view my appointments, prescriptions, reports, and bills so that I can stay informed about my care.
As a nurse, I want to manage bed allocation and track patient admissions/discharges so that resources are optimized.
As an admin, I want to manage staff profiles and roles so that personnel records are up-to-date.
Facilitates HR operations and role-based access.
As an admin, I want to track hospital inventory and manage procurement so that supplies are always available.
Prevents operational disruptions due to stock shortages.
As a user, I want to receive notifications for appointments, test results, and system alerts so that I am kept informed.
As an admin, I want to review audit logs and ensure data validation so that system integrity and compliance are maintained.
Supports HIPAA/GDPR compliance and security monitoring.
As an admin, I want to generate reports and view dashboards so that I can monitor hospital performance.

sections.title: 3. Release Slicing & Implementation Dependencies
sections.body:
**Release Slicing:**
- **Release 1 (Core Operations):** Authentication (US-001), Patient Management (US-002), Appointment Scheduling (US-003), EMR (US-004), Billing (US-007).
- **Release 2 (Clinical Support):** Laboratory Management (US-005), Pharmacy Management (US-006), Bed & Ward Management (US-009), Patient Portal (US-008).
- **Release 3 (Administrative & Compliance):** Staff Management (US-010), Inventory & Procurement (US-011), Notifications (US-012), Audit Logs (US-013), Reports (US-014).

**Implementation Dependencies:**
1. **Authentication (US-001)** must be completed before any role-specific features can be implemented.
2. **Patient Management (US-002)** is a prerequisite for Appointment Scheduling (US-003) and EMR (US-004).
3. **EMR (US-004)** depends on Patient Management and is required for Laboratory (US-005) and Pharmacy (US-006) workflows.
4. **Billing (US-007)** depends on Appointment Scheduling, EMR, Laboratory, and Pharmacy modules to generate accurate invoices.
5. **Audit Logs (US-013)** should be integrated early to ensure compliance from the start, but full reporting can be deferred to Release 3.
6. **Patient Portal (US-008)** depends on the completion of EMR, Billing, and Appointment modules to provide accurate data to patients.

**Open Items:**
- Specific integration details with external insurance providers are not specified in the source document and require stakeholder input.
- Detailed HL7 FHIR/DICOM integration requirements for medical records and imaging are not explicitly outlined and need further clarification.

File: A Hospital Management System.pdf
--- Page 1 ---
Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
